title: Settlement Economy: production, consumption and trade of goods
about: The implementation plan for the design statement (statement.md): components with features; each feature names the code it changes, its ordered tasks, the data it adds, the features it comes after, what the player can verify, and the checks that say it is done. tools/check_plan.py validates the plan, confirms every anchor in the mod source, runs the audits and reports progress; --summary works without a checkout. Anchors are literal text in the mod checkout (GitLab main); 'added' checks are text the work adds.

statement.summary: Resources stop being map tokens a civilization has or lacks. They become goods in physical quantities, produced by each settlement from the land it works, its improvements, buildings, specialists and population, consumed in proportion to its size and way of life. Surpluses and shortages drive growth, contentment, industry, trade and war. Diplomacy moves from leasing a resource for gold per turn to real commerce: shipping goods, selling seeds and breeding stock, multi-part contracts.
principles: P1 Physical quantities: every good is counted in units that mean something (tonnes, bales, barrels, crates) and is conserved: made, moved, stored, used up or spoiled.

P2 Production comes from the whole settlement: worked tiles and their improvements, buildings, specialists and available labour. Land sets what is possible; people and capital set how much is realised.
P3 Consumption comes from population: needs per citizen rise with size and with era.
P4 Industry transforms goods at defined rates; the scarcest input limits the result.
P5 Military power has a material cost: units cost production and goods; armies in the field use supplies.
P6 Trade carries the goods themselves: goods, the means to produce them, money and treaties, in deals of any shape.
P7 The simulation lives in the DLL; XML holds the data; Python shows it.

decisions.question: Scale of units
decisions.choice: Real quantities in whole integers, each good in its own unit (tonnes, bales, barrels, crates), sized so no value can overflow; never shown as a fulfilment ratio.

decisions.question: Food
decisions.choice: Staple food is a good in tonnes. A city eats first and grows from its surplus; citizens starve only when stores are empty. Spoilage of food depends on the preservation technologies the owner lacks.

decisions.question: Number of goods
decisions.choice: The game's existing resource types are the goods, as they are now; no new goods for now.

decisions.question: Need tiers
decisions.choice: Needs grow along two building chains the game already has. The essentials buildings (Settlement, Town, City, Metropolitan) set how much a citizen needs of the basics (staple food, fuel, clothing). The market chain (Market, Fair, Commodity Market, Commercial Center, Hypermarket) sets which further goods a citizen wants and how much (variety, comforts, luxuries). Technological progression raises output through the techs' existing yield changes.

decisions.question: Distribution
decisions.choice: As the game works now: goods are shared across a connected trade network (CvPlotGroup: roads, rivers, coast). Blockades count: enemy ships blockading water plots take them out of the network (CvUnit::updatePlunder, CvPlot::isTradeNetwork), which changes what reaches a city and what deliveries arrive. Transport limits apply only to units (their cargo), not to goods.

decisions.question: Contracts and the trade screen
decisions.choice: Modify the executable's diplomacy screen through the DLL (item list and item text); no separate trade screen.

decisions.question: Order of work
decisions.choice: Geography and the way tiles work first (component LQ), then the goods accounts and production.

decisions.question: Icons
decisions.choice: Every good keeps its icon; no icon is missing or shared; any icon added later loads its own glyph, button and art define.

decisions.question: Wool
options: sheep pastures yield wool beside meat and dairy
decisions.why: Nothing places, gives or uses BONUS_WOOL today (catalogue.json), yet clothing needs it

decisions.question: Resources that are not physical goods
options: outside the goods accounts: Drama, Music, Movies stay building-given resources; Ancient Temple and Thermal Vent stay map sites
decisions.why: They are culture given by buildings or sites with no improvement that trades them (catalogue.json)

decisions.question: Fuel before coal
options: the fuel need starts with coal (its era)
forests yield a fuel good, which needs one new resource type despite D3
decisions.proposal: the fuel need starts with coal
decisions.why: No timber or wood resource exists; the existing fuel goods are coal, oil, uranium, diesel, methane, biofuel and whale (catalogue.json)

decisions.question: Clothing in the early game
options: wool (D10), fur and cotton are the clothing goods
the clothing need starts once two of them are available
decisions.why: These are the only existing clothing goods (catalogue.json)

components.title: Geography and tiles
components.player_sees: No resource tokens on the map. The land itself has qualities: crop and herd suitability, ore grade and depth, fishing grounds, shown in the plot help and a map overlay. What a tile yields follows its qualities and the improvement built on it; the improvement decides which of the plot's qualities it uses (a farm the crops, a pasture the herds, a mine the ore). Techs keep adding yield as they do now. A city still gains a resource as today, from an improved, connected tile, but the tile's quality is the source instead of a placed token.

resume: The plan, not memory or a summary, holds the task structure. A new or compacted session starts here.
1. Read statement.md (the design) and the decisions in plan.json; open decisions show the proposal to put to the user.
2. Run tools/check_plan.py --summary (no checkout needed): progress, the next component, the features that can start and their tasks.
3. With a mod checkout: tools/catalogue.py and tools/callsites.py to refresh the generated files, then tools/check_plan.py <checkout> to refresh status.json.
4. Work only on features the summary lists as able to start; a feature is done when its checks pass.
5. A new decision, a changed feature or a reclassified call site goes into the plan files in the same commit as the work, with status.json refreshed.
